author: s. l. mendes
title: Troy's College World Series run ends with loss to West Virginia - Wiregrass Times
text:
Troy University’s baseball team ended its 2026 season with a 12-0 defeat against No. 16 national seed West Virginia in the College World Series elimination game in Omaha, Neb., on June 16.
The Trojans concluded their postseason with a 7-3 record in the NCAA Tournament. After losing their regional opener, Troy won four straight games to secure the Gainesville Regional, swept Little Rock in the first-ever Troy Super Regional, and finished 1-2 at Omaha. The run included the program’s first College World Series victory over Ole Miss on Sunday.
In Tuesday’s matchup, West Virginia starter Dawson Montesa limited Troy to two hits over 5.1 innings while striking out six and walking four. Three Mountaineer relievers combined to allow just two more hits and three walks for the remainder of the game. Troy starter Cooper Ellingworth pitched three innings, giving up two runs on four hits and three walks while striking out four batters.
Ellingworth kept West Virginia scoreless through two innings but surrendered a pair of two-out runs in the third after an RBI double by Matthew Graveline, followed by a walk, hit batter, and wild pitch. Dylan Alonso entered in relief for Troy, pitching 2.2 innings with two hits allowed and five strikeouts but gave up four runs after consecutive walks set up Gavin Kelly’s three-run home run for West Virginia.
Matt Dill took over from Alonso following an infield single by Paul Schoenfeld; Schoenfeld later scored on a wild pitch and Sean Smith’s single to extend West Virginia’s lead to 6-0. The Mountaineers added one run in the seventh inning and five more in the ninth as Troy used three additional pitchers out of its bullpen. Overall, West Virginia out-hit Troy by a margin of 14-4.
